name: Chigua (吃瓜)
blurb: Chinese slang for "eating melon": watching gossip and drama from the sidelines
title: Chigua (吃瓜) Meaning: "Eating Melon" in Chinese Slang
description: Chigua (吃瓜), "eating melon", is Chinese slang for watching gossip or drama from the sidelines. Onlookers are the 吃瓜群众, or melon eaters.
answer: Chigua (吃瓜, chī guā), "eating melon", means following gossip, scandals or online drama as a bystander, watching without taking part or taking sides, much like "grabbing the popcorn". The onlookers are 吃瓜群众, "the melon-eating masses", and 瓜 (melon) itself now means a piece of gossip. 吃瓜群众 was one of the language magazine 咬文嚼字's top 10 buzzwords of 2016.

body: A common explanation is that on online forums, people who just watched an argument without posting were pictured cracking melon seeds on the sidelines; this shortened to 吃瓜, and the watchers became 吃瓜群众.

The phrase exploded in 2016, when 咬文嚼字 named 吃瓜群众 one of its top 10 buzzwords, noting that people use it to tease themselves or others for staying out of things and only watching. Since then 瓜 alone has come to mean gossip or news.

ul: 前排吃瓜，坐等反转 (front-row seat, waiting for the plot twist)
今天微博又有大瓜，你看了吗？ (there's huge gossip on Weibo today, seen it?)
我就是个吃瓜群众，不站队 (I'm just a bystander, not picking sides)
这瓜保熟吗？ (is this melon ripe?, i.e. is this rumour true?)
吃瓜吃到自己公司头上了 (the gossip turned out to be about my own company)

head: Term
Meaning
rows: onlookers, ordinary netizens watching the drama
the person the gossip is about
the gossip turns out to involve you

body: Chigua is lighthearted, but online "melons" are often unverified. Check sources before sharing, don't present rumours as fact, and never dig up or harass the people involved.
Saying 吃瓜 about disasters or tragedies sounds callous; avoid it there.

faq.q: What does 吃瓜群众 mean?
faq.a: "The melon-eating masses": ordinary internet users who watch gossip or a controversy without commenting. It was a 2016 buzzword of the year.

faq.q: What does 瓜 (melon) mean in Chinese slang?
faq.a: A piece of gossip, scandal or trending news. 有瓜 means "there's some gossip".
"Grabbing the popcorn" or "watching the drama unfold" are the closest.
